flags.claim: Claude Code can call OpenAI by running the OpenAI Codex CLI as an MCP server (`codex mcp-server`).
flags.correction: OpenAI's current docs state the codex mcp-server command and the standalone codex-mcp-server binary have been removed; the replacement app server uses JSON-RPC (not MCP) and is experimental. Use openai/codex-plugin-cc, `codex exec` via Bash, or the read-only Docs MCP.
flags.detail: The docs give no removal version or date, so installed Codex versions may differ. Community wrappers around the CLI and third-party blog posts from May 2026 still describe MCP server use; they were not opened and should not be relied on.

flags.claim: OpenAI file_search citations (file_id, filename, text index) can be re-anchored to clause level by string match.
flags.correction: Send Docling clause passages inline and require verbatim quotes in a strict JSON field, then exact-match each quote in code; or set include file_search_call.results and align claims to the returned chunks with a fuzzy tolerance. Show OpenAI-route claims as UNVERIFIED until they resolve. Normaliser re-estimated at ~2 days instead of 4.
flags.detail: The file_citation index is the position in the model's output text where the citation is inserted (API reference), not an offset into the source, and the annotation carries no quoted text; search results are returned only when requested through include. Evidence: P16-S59, P16-S12.

flags.claim: Exceeding the Higher Buildings Policy 'may be considered' 600 ft (183 m) height is discretionary and returns 'needs justification', not a breach.
flags.correction: Below 183 m: Permission (may be considered, not approval). Above 183 m: the tower exceeds the policy's height limits, so record a departure from policy as a justified-departure item (the brief invites justified breaches). Whether the VTC site lies inside the policy area stays UNRESOLVED; the derived limit card (Prohibition, defeasible) stays UNVERIFIED until the policy text is read.
flags.detail: City FAQ (P16-S37): within the policy area buildings up to 600ft (183 m) may be considered; the Bay Parkade towers exceed the heights contemplated by the policy, do not conform to its height limits and seek exceptions to them. The critique quoted the word 'ceiling'; that word did not appear on the page as fetched (summary read), but 'height limits' and 'exceptions' support the same conclusion. The supporting sentence concerns a site outside the policy area (r2 note). The policy PDF remains unread.

flags.claim: LegalRuleML strict / defeasible / defeater correspond to deontic strength shall / should / may.
flags.correction: Keep two separate card fields: deontic_type (obligation, prohibition, permission, right) and strength (strict, defeasible, defeater).
flags.detail: LegalRuleML 1.0 section 3.4 defines strict, defeasible and defeater as rule strength, and Obligation, Prohibition, Permission and Right as deontic specifications; section 4.2.3.1 gives the operators [OBL], [PER], [FOR]. Evidence: P16-S29.

flags.claim: Prompts under 512 tokens are not cached on 5.x models (that is, all 5.x models have a 512 minimum).
flags.correction: Keep the minimum cacheable length per model id in the versioned capability table; note that caches are isolated per workspace.
flags.detail: Claude Sonnet 5 needs 1,024 tokens; 512 applies to Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Opus 5, Fable and Mythos 5 and 5.1. Evidence: P16-S04.

flags.claim: The provider retention to plan for is Anthropic 30-day deletion and OpenAI 30-day abuse-monitoring logs.
flags.correction: Set store:false on every OpenAI Responses call; never send feedback ratings; batch, files and vector stores only for public or planted data, with a scheduled deletion job; keep a per-feature retention table in the capability matrix.
flags.detail: OpenAI also keeps Responses state 30 days by default and its files, vector stores, batches and conversations persist until deleted outside ZDR. Anthropic keeps flagged content up to 2 years, feedback 5 years, Batch 29 days (not ZDR) and Files API until deleted. Evidence: P16-S14, P16-S07, P16-S08.

flags.claim: The jury weights 40/30/20/10 are 'verified'.
flags.correction: The weights are a team assumption until a person opens the brief PDF and reviews the brief card; the VTC brief is now source P16-S58 (opened=false).
flags.detail: P16-M05 labelled the sum verified with empty source_ids and a basis saying the PDF was not re-opened; the packet's own rule requires a source plus a reviewer for verified.

flags.claim: The W3C Web Annotation model establishes that TextQuoteSelector survives re-pagination.
flags.correction: Present 'survives re-pagination' as team reasoning; cite W3C only for exact/prefix/suffix and for TextPositionSelector being very brittle.
flags.detail: The text read does not discuss pagination; it says TextPositionSelector is very brittle to changes and defines prefix and suffix as the snippets before and after the quoted text. Evidence: P16-S28.

flags.claim: The Okabe-Ito page gives vermilion as #FF2000 (a reliable hex anchor), and its palette hexes can be used without a contrast check.
flags.correction: Treat all palette hexes, vermilion included, as team presets checked for contrast in both themes; light-theme team assumption uses #B86B00 instead of #E69F00 (superseded by the r2 palette in P16-M03).
flags.detail: The page states 'RGB=100%,32%,0% or #FF2000', but 32% green is about 82, giving #FF5200; no other hexes are in the page text. Computed in r1: #E69F00 on white is 2.25:1, below the 3:1 the spec requires. Evidence: P16-S41, P16-S40.

flags.claim: The Codex CLI licence is unverified.
flags.correction: Record Apache-2.0 and pin the version; install on Windows with npm at a pinned version rather than the piped PowerShell installer.
flags.detail: The openai/codex repository states Apache-2.0 (opened r1); its documented Windows installer pipes a remote script and its Windows support level is not stated. Evidence: P16-S62.

flags.claim: Credential variables are not expanded in remote URLs or headers of project-scoped MCP servers (P16-M07).
flags.correction: Treat ${OPENAI_API_KEY} or ${CODEX_API_KEY} in .mcp.json as live secrets that may be sent. Keep remote servers that use secrets out of project scope (use user or local scope), start CI and -p runs with --strict-mcp-config or disabledMcpjsonServers, put .mcp.json and .claude/** under CODEOWNERS, and test with a planted .mcp.json (P16-M08).
flags.detail: The Claude Code MCP docs blank only named credential categories (Claude Code's own such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, cloud-provider credentials, and others such as HTTPS_PROXY and NPM_TOKEN) in a remote server's url and headers; a name outside the set, such as API_KEY, expands as written, and no full list is given. The same docs say claude -p, Agent SDK and cloud sessions load project servers without approval. So a pull request that changes a committed URL could send a key to a named host. Evidence: P16-S20 (re-read r2), P16-S77.

flags.claim: The Higher Buildings Policy PDF cannot be obtained (only via guidelines.vancouver.ca, HTTP 403).
flags.correction: The City's Shape Your City project page links a second copy titled 'Higher Buildings Policy (PDF 0.9 MB)'. A team member downloads it manually, records SHA-256, edition and date, and reviews the height, policy-area and criteria clauses; then S38/S78 are updated and the derived limit card is confirmed or corrected. If that download also fails, the attempt goes in the change log.
flags.detail: Project page key documents (opened r2) list the link https://www.shapeyourcity.ca/51604/widgets/218772/documents/166245. WebFetch of that link returned only an HTML 'download will begin' page with a blank filename, and guidelines.vancouver.ca returned 403 again, so the text itself is still unread and the clause-level claims remain UNVERIFIED. Evidence: P16-S60, P16-S78, P16-S38.

flags.claim: An exact-string match of the stored quote in the source text resolves an anchor (100% resolution target).
flags.correction: Count a quote as resolved only when exact+prefix+suffix gives exactly one match inside the expected clause; show zero or several matches as UNVERIFIED and report unique, ambiguous and unmatched counts separately.
flags.detail: W3C Web Annotation section 4.2.4: if prefix, exact and suffix together match more than one text sequence, the selection should be treated as matching all of them, so finding the string does not give one location. Repeated phrases such as 'may be considered' occur more than once on the City FAQ. Evidence: P16-S28 (re-read r2).

flags.claim: One OpenAI-compatible interface is enough for a provider-neutral adapter.
flags.correction: Anthropic states its compatibility layer is for testing, ignores file inputs and strict schemas, lacks prompt caching, and omits citations; native SDKs behind one typed interface are needed.
flags.detail: Citation formats also differ: Claude returns document or search_result locations; OpenAI returns file_id, filename and an index into the output text.

flags.claim: Rule extraction can use Claude citations and strict JSON output in a single call.
flags.correction: Claude returns HTTP 400 when citations are enabled together with structured outputs, and structured outputs cannot enforce numeric min/max (and cap optional parameters at 24); use two calls and validate numbers in code.
flags.detail: OpenAI strict json_schema has its own subset limits; check before porting schemas.

flags.claim: A cheaper second LLM call that checks entailment can label a cited claim 'verified'.
flags.correction: CitedClaim.support is now anchored, machine_entailed or not_supported; a verified chip requires a reviewer id, and LLM-only support is capped at UNVERIFIED.
flags.detail: Anthropic guarantees that citation pointers are valid, not that the quote entails the claim; a machine check labelled verified would pass LLM judgment off as human review.

flags.claim: A later contradicting source moves a value straight to FALSE ASSUMPTION.
flags.correction: A contradicting source moves the value to UNRESOLVED; only a reviewer sets FALSE ASSUMPTION, and any dependant shows 'depends on FALSE ASSUMPTION' and is blocked from board export.
flags.detail: The earlier rule bypassed human review and left propagation from a FALSE input undefined; unresolved ranks below unverified because it blocks a pass/fail judgement.

flags.claim: A reviewer id (and a self-ticked 'source opened' box) is enough to make a card or claim verified.
flags.correction: Verified brief and policy cards need reviewer_id different from proposer_id, a blind-first review, a third-person audit of about 10% of cards and seeded wrong cards that must be rejected; the bar is renamed 'k of N samples agree', not confidence.
flags.detail: Self-review by the person who ran the extraction removes the check in a two-student team; automation-bias reviews list accountability and training as mitigators and an online study of 199 participants found cognitive forcing reduced overreliance. Neither source tests rule-card review. Evidence: P16-S67, P16-S68.

flags.claim: One status per value, ranked verified > team assumption > unverified > unresolved, is enough.
flags.correction: Flags carry three facets (fidelity, interpretation, applicability); the chip shows the worst, the drawer names the open facet; team assumption and unverified are incomparable tiers listed together; attaching a source never lowers a badge.
flags.detail: A single status mixed three questions (quote match, human reading, site applicability) and ranked an unsourced preset above an anchored, machine-checked claim, which rewards leaving values unsourced. The new ordering is still a team design choice; designers' comprehension is tested in P16-M08.

flags.claim: A FALSE-dependent result may be exported to a board once a rationale is recorded in P16-M04.
flags.correction: One rule in P16-M03, M04 and M05: a FALSE-dependent figure is never exported unmarked; a rationale unlocks only the corrected value or the wrong value drawn 'superseded, shown for comparison'.
flags.detail: The r1 wording contradicted the packet's own metric of zero such exports and its rule that a board must not show a number marked wrong. A control case in P16-M08 tries the loophole.

flags.claim: AI-drafted rationale can be labelled until the user edits it, after which it counts as the user's rationale.
flags.correction: Every rationale and card field stores a permanent authorship record (origin, editor, edit_ratio); the 'AI-drafted, edited by' label never clears and the AI-use statement counts it; AI drafting is off by default and the tool writes no rationale answers.
flags.detail: A one-character edit would otherwise relabel AI text as human and under-report AI use, contradicting the rule that the tool never invents a rationale.

flags.claim: A weighted jury score with 'rank-1 unchanged in >=90% of draws' helps choose between options.
flags.correction: Grey the weighted aggregate when over 50% (preset) of the weight rests on manual or non-verified inputs; report rank acceptability per option and frontier-membership stability instead of a winner; draw weights from a stated Dirichlet; define clipping and direction.
flags.detail: Human scale (40) and cultural context (30) are mostly qualitative ratings, so a single number gives false precision, and a rank-1 metric names a winner in practice. Pareto membership does not depend on weights, so frontier stability perturbs thresholds, not weights. Evidence: P16-S70, P16-S71.

flags.claim: Clause-level content of the Higher Buildings Policy (1997, last updated 2011) beyond the 600 ft (183 m) 'may be considered' statement and the FAQ's 'height limits' wording.
flags.detail: guidelines.vancouver.ca returned HTTP 403 in r1 and r2, as did the engagement PDF on syc.vancouver.ca. The Shape Your City project page links a second copy (P16-S78), but WebFetch returned only a download-redirect page, so the text is unread. Only the Shape Your City FAQ and project page were opened. flags.claim: VTC brief facts used in cards and test cases (9.0 FSR non-residential minimum, 244-305 m range, jury weights 40/30/20/10, four A2 boards, justified-breach allowance).

unresolved_relationships: Chunk size (clause vs sentence vs page) -> citation precision and anchor resolution on Vancouver policy PDFs: no sourced study found; measure with P16-M08 once the policy PDF is obtainable.
Number of independent samples N -> calibration of agreement-based confidence for clause extraction: consistency sampling helps in general, but no value of N for this task is established.
Disagreement between Claude and OpenAI -> probability that a rule card is wrong: not sourced (S36 covers samples from one model only); to be measured.
Relative citation accuracy of Claude search_result blocks versus OpenAI inline verbatim-quote JSON on municipal policy text: no comparative study found.
Showing evidence flags and provenance -> change in how designers make decisions or how a jury reads boards: no evidence found; P16-M08 human track will give first counts only.
Prompt-injection success rate versus defences for ingested policy PDFs: no portable figure found.
Effect of a justified breach of policy on jury scoring: the brief says breaches may be rewarded but gives no rule or weight.
Mapping from module metrics to the four jury criteria (human scale, cultural context, design excellence, urban integration): team judgment only; no source defines it.

Whether the 1997 policy text states 183 m as a hard limit, a guideline for consideration, or an area-specific cap: the policy PDF is unread (a second copy is linked on the City project page but returned only a download page); the City FAQ's 'height limits' and 'heights contemplated' wording is the only source.
Embedding model choice (local voyage-4-nano vs OpenAI text-embedding-3-small) -> retrieval recall on Vancouver policy text: no study found.

Worst-input propagation with two incomparable middle tiers -> share of results that end up amber or UNRESOLVED in practice and whether the badges stay useful: unmeasured; P16-M08 badge-informativeness metric will report it.
Machine entailment check accuracy on municipal clauses compared with human labels: unmeasured; use the P16-M08 gold set.

Blind-first review and seeded wrong cards -> reviewer error rate on rule cards in a two-student team: the sources (a 199-participant online study and a clinical review) cover other tasks; no figure for rule-card review.
Reviewer dwell time -> review quality: no source; the tool logs it only as an audit trigger, never as proof of attention.
Three-facet flag versus a single chip -> designers' comprehension and speed: unmeasured; the legend-comprehension study in P16-M08 gives first counts.
Perturbation range of team-assumption thresholds (preset +/-10% of the good-bad span) -> realistic uncertainty in frontier membership: unsourced.
Share of options that stay non-dominated as the number of metrics grows: no sourced figure for this tool; the Pareto set is computed on the four roll-up criteria first for that reason.

Capture burden of a one-line rationale at defined decision events -> completeness and quality of rationale in this tool: only qualitative support (design-rationale literature via S69); measured in P16-M08.

notes:
Scope: P16 modules do not score a tower; jury tags show which criteria they support indirectly. r2 headline changes: (1) a verified rule card now needs a second person, a blind-first review, an audit sample and seeded wrong cards; (2) flags carry three facets (fidelity, interpretation, applicability) so a chip names the open question; (3) one export rule everywhere: a FALSE-marked number is never exported unmarked, and a rationale cannot change that; (4) authorship records stay on every rationale and card field; (5) the weighted jury score is greyed when most of the weight rests on manual or non-verified inputs; (6) the MCP credential statement was corrected and agent configuration gets CODEOWNERS and strict-MCP guards; (7) entry projects and traces are private until winners are announced; (8) the City's second copy of the Higher Buildings Policy is recorded but still unread, so the derived height-limit card stays UNVERIFIED; (9) a small human-centred evaluation measures whether designers read the flags correctly.

Schedule: today is 21 Oct 2026; the course cut is 13 Nov (23 calendar days, about 16 working days: team assumption). VTC registration closes 29 Oct 2026 and submissions close 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London time (competition page). If P16 gets about one third of two students' time (team assumption, roughly 10-11 person-days), the 13 Nov slice is M01 ~5.5 d, M02 manual cards ~2.5 d, M03 ~2.5 d, M04 log and timeline ~2.5-3 d, M07 ~1.5 d = about 14.5-15 d, so about 4 days over. Cut order if short: M04 timeline UI (~1), M01 viewer highlight polish (~1), M02 review pane polish (~0.5), M03 ledger and graph (~0.5); that still leaves about 1-2 days, so P16's share must rise or M07's CODEOWNERS and CI flags move to the week after. Do not cut the schema-level controls (three facets, proposer and reviewer ids, authorship records, the single export rule, private-by-default visibility): they are cheap now and costly to retrofit into an append-only log. Everything LLM-assisted (retrieval, cited Q&A, extraction, adapter, evaluation, option comparison) lands by 10 Dec. The source count (78) exceeds the ~40 guide because each platform claim (price, retention, licence, removal of codex mcp-server, brief and terms, MCP credential rules) needs its own primary page.

Privacy rules (revised r2): (1) default to public source text and summarised metrics; raw Layer 0 geometry, file metadata or personal data leave the machine only after explicit opt-in; (2) strip author, account, EXIF/XMP, file-name and trace identifiers from every payload and export because VTC entries must not identify entrants (Terms 5.1, 5.3) and panels are JPEG under 10 MB (4.8); (3) set store:false on every OpenAI Responses call, never send feedback ratings, and use batch, files and vector stores only for public or planted data with a logged deletion job; (4) retention to plan for: Anthropic deletes inputs and outputs within 30 days, flagged content up to 2 years, feedback 5 years, Batch 29 days (not ZDR), Files API until deleted; Covered Models (Fable and Mythos 5 and 5.1) require 30-day retention and are outside ZDR; OpenAI keeps Responses state 30 days unless store:false, abuse logs up to 30 days, files, vector stores, batches and conversations until deleted and outside ZDR, Canada storage-only; neither provider trains on API data by default; (5) log prompt hashes and usage, and store prompt and response text only in the user's own trace; (6) do not ingest Indigenous or community knowledge without community permission (TCPS 2 chapter 9, OCAP); (7) respect document licences before any provider upload; (8) keys server-side or session-only, never in browser storage, git, project-scope MCP urls or headers, or community modules; (9) community-uploaded documents and forked modules are untrusted by default, with canary scanning, no-tool calls, schema-validated outputs, per-module budgets; (10) on provider outage, show stored results marked offline; (11) entry projects, Layer 0 snapshots and traces are private by default until winners are announced, and only modules can be published; (12) human-centred studies need the ethics route settled first (instructor, UBC research ethics; TCPS 2 Article 2.5 is the likely basis, not a ruling); (13) non-public data classes do not go to Covered Models without opt-in. The governing privacy statute (BC FIPPA via UBC, PIPA or PIPEDA) is unresolved (see flags).

Key facts used: Higher Buildings Policy established 1997, last updated 2011; within its policy area buildings up to 600 ft (183 m) may be considered; towers above exceed its height limits (City FAQ); review phases run from spring 2026 to Council in 2027 with the FAQ and project page differing on Phase 2 timing; protected public views are outside the review (project page); 600 ft = 182.88 m, 800-1000 ft = 243.84-304.8 m. Web search was exhausted in r2 too, so all research used page fetches. Several pages (TCPS 2, competition terms, some OpenAI pages) were read through automatic summaries.
